headline: Funding flows. Procurement reshuffles. Startups surge.
deck: This week saw significant funding rounds and strategic shifts in procurement across the space sector.

stories.head: True Anomaly secures $190M Series C funding
stories.body: True Anomaly has raised $190 million in Series C funding, valuing the co-orbital security startup at $1.6 billion. The investment underscores the Department of Defense's growing interest in space domain awareness solutions. This round follows a trend of increased defense spending on advanced technologies, particularly in the face of rising geopolitical tensions.
stories.soWhat: With the DoD's pull-through, True Anomaly is positioning itself as a key player in a market that’s becoming increasingly crowded but still lucrative.

stories.head: Space Force reorganizes for streamlined acquisitions
stories.body: The Space Force has completed a major procurement reorganization, establishing nine new acquisition portfolios to enhance oversight on modernization decisions. This shift is aimed at improving efficiency and aligning procurement strategies with current mission requirements. The move comes as the Space Force seeks to adapt to rapidly evolving technological landscapes.
stories.soWhat: Expect a more agile procurement process, which could favor startups that can pivot quickly to meet new requirements—if they can survive the bureaucratic maze.

stories.head: Pulse Space awarded $40M for laser power tech
stories.body: Pulse Space has been awarded a $40 million contract by the Space Force to develop laser systems for power and data transmission between spacecraft. This funding is part of a broader push towards innovative energy solutions in space, highlighting the military's interest in harnessing cutting-edge technology for operational advantages.
stories.soWhat: If Pulse Space can deliver, we might see a shift in how we think about power distribution in orbit—no more relying solely on solar panels.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on SpaceX's IPO developments
watchlist.body: With SpaceX's valuation hitting $470 billion, the IPO buzz could bring new capital into the sector, reshaping investment dynamics.

watchlist.title: Upcoming budget discussions for FY27
watchlist.body: The additional $1.4 billion for space resilience in the FY27 budget could lead to new contracts and opportunities for agile startups.

watchlist.title: Watch for Palantir's TITAN program updates
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN ground station program may signal further government reliance on commercial data solutions.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's next steps post-design review
watchlist.body: With the Dream Chaser DoD variant passing its design review, watch for updates on its launch timeline and potential customers.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
